findings.finding: The ambiguity error lists eight-character pair prefixes but requires a full pair id from that list; its suggested action is not executable as printed. Identical names alone do not establish that one live target is stale.

An absent active registry entry is treated as a retired pair without checking retirement evidence. Unknown pair ids and sender identities inconsistent with archived pairs were injected. Retired-message handling must preserve the original pair identity checks.

After a retired message is consumed, its repeated wake is not suppressed because the branch requires an active pair. No duplicate body was injected, but the hook incorrectly reports missing pending/consumption evidence.

After the last pair is retired with an accepted message pending, a different Codex identity can be paired in the same root. The hook then rejects the original Codex session and leaves its old message pending. The chosen lifecycle policy must prevent or handle this transition explicitly.

The committed test completes publish before retiring, despite describing retirement between lookup and publication. Its foreign-recipient check also runs after the pending message has already been consumed. The independent interleaving check does deliver correctly; committed regression should reproduce the actual boundary.
